analysis.title: Oil price swings put energy equity valuations to the test (UBS House View - Daily EMEA)
key_insights: Brent and WTI ended October up 13.6% and 15.2%, the fourth consecutive monthly gain, with renewed tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent fell to around USD 105/bbl in the last two days of the report window on hopes for US-Iran diplomatic progress, while the US resumed 'defensive strikes' on Qeshm Island.

The early-November decline removed part of oil's geopolitical risk premium but says little about physical market conditions. Combined crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz and bypass pipelines were estimated at more than 17.3mbpd in September and close to 18.8mbpd in the first three weeks of October, versus 19.9mbpd before the conflict.

The inventory buffer has shrunk. Global visible oil inventories fell by slightly more than 500 million barrels between February and September per IEA data, mostly from strategic reserves. Middle East-to-China VLCC freight is around USD 30-40 per barrel versus USD 1-3/bbl over the previous decade, and recovering Chinese crude imports remove another shock absorber.

UBS forecasts Brent at USD 110/bbl at year-end 2026, USD 95 in March 2027, USD 90 in June and USD 85 in September. Risks stay elevated and depend on the Middle East conflict, US-Iran diplomacy and the pace of Gulf production, shipping and demand recovery.

UBS keeps Neutral ratings on both European and US energy sectors. Spot oil is an unreliable guide to equity returns, and after the gains already made, selectivity matters more than adding broad sector exposure.

US energy: the S&P 500 Energy Index is up 59.9% YTD on a total-return basis versus 11.8% for the S&P 500. US managers kept capital discipline, directing cash to debt reduction, buybacks and dividends.

Valuation limits upside for US energy. The index trades at about 7.3x expected 2027 EV/EBITDA versus a three-year average of 6.7x. The 2027 consensus free-cash-flow yield is 8.0% and the dividend yield is 2.4%. Energy is roughly 4% of the S&P 500 and UBS sees a similar portfolio weight as appropriate.

Within US energy UBS rates oil and gas equipment and services Attractive (international and offshore spending expected to accelerate in 2027, energy security focus) and oil and gas storage and transportation Attractive (rising pipeline volumes, manageable capex, strong balance sheets).

European energy: defensiveness, strong balance sheets, and integrated oil companies' refining and marketing profits and gas conditions support the sector. High crude prices, refining margins and the risk premium are already in earnings expectations and valuations, and lower spot oil could temper near-term earnings expectations if diplomacy continues.

UBS recommends diversified commodity exposure across precious metals, energy, industrial metals and agriculture instead of adding broadly to energy equities, favoring an actively managed approach. It cites inflation protection, low correlation with traditional assets, electrification, power demand, AI infrastructure and supply constraints.

US midterms on Tuesday 3 November: all 435 House seats, 35 of 100 Senate seats and 36 governorships are up. Trump's net approval is -20pps and Democrats lead the generic ballot by 8.9pps in the RCP average.

UBS midterm probabilities: 50% Democrats win both chambers, 40% Democrats win the House with Republicans keeping the Senate, 10% Republicans keep both. UBS does not expect the result to derail data-center expansion, and sees possible debt-ceiling volatility in 2027. It says not to treat the midterms as a binary directional event and that earnings, AI investment, inflation and rates matter more.

sector_views.rationale: Valuations at 7.3x 2027 EV/EBITDA versus a 6.7x three-year average, after a 59.9% YTD gain, support Neutral over a broad overweight. The 8.0% FCF yield stays attractive.
Higher crude, refining margins and the risk premium are already reflected in earnings expectations and valuations.

sector_views.sector: US Oil and Gas Equipment and Services
sector_views.rationale: International spending expected to accelerate in 2027 as investment broadens across international and offshore markets, supported by energy security focus. UBS rates it Attractive.

sector_views.sector: US Oil and Gas Storage and Transportation
sector_views.rationale: Rising pipeline volumes, manageable capital expenditure and strong balance sheets. UBS rates it Attractive.
Structural return source and protection if higher inflation expectations challenge equities and bonds. Supported by electrification, power demand, AI infrastructure and supply constraints.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher crude improves producer operating conditions, US managers kept capital discipline, and the 8.0% 2027 FCF yield and 2.4% dividend yield stay attractive. Integrated European firms gain from refining margins and gas.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy is up 59.9% YTD, the index trades at 7.3x 2027 EV/EBITDA versus a 6.7x three-year average, and lower spot oil from US-Iran diplomacy could temper earnings expectations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued diplomatic breakthrough lowering spot oil would temper near-term earnings expectations and weaken the bull case.
